items.followUp: A block has a mass of 600 g and a volume of 150 cm³. Find its density in kg/m³.

rubric.why: Correctly converts the given mass and volume to SI units.
rubric.description: Convert mass and volume to SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for m = 0.8 kg and V = 2 × 10⁻⁴ m³ (or 0.0002 m³).

rubric.why: Uses the density relation and obtains the correct SI answer.
rubric.description: Calculate density and state it with its SI unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct density calculation and 4000 kg/m³.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 800 g = 0.8 kg; V = 200 cm³ = 2 × 10⁻⁴ m³
Formula: ρ = m/V
Substitution: ρ = 0.8 kg ÷ (2 × 10⁻⁴ m³)
Answer: ρ = 4000 kg/m³

items.followUp: Define the center of gravity and state how it is related to the center of mass.

rubric.why: A correct definition identifies the point where the body's mass can be treated as concentrated.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that it is the point at which the whole mass of a body may be considered concentrated.

modelAnswer: The center of mass of a body is the point at which its whole mass may be considered concentrated.

items.followUp: Define one watt and write the formula for power.

rubric.why: The definition specifies the work done by a one-newton force over one metre in its direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one joule is the work done when a force of 1 N moves an object 1 m in the direction of the force.

rubric.why: The formula expresses work as force multiplied by displacement in the direction of the force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for W = Fd (or an equivalent expression).

modelAnswer: One joule is the work done when a force of 1 N moves an object 1 m in the direction of the force.
Formula: W = Fd

items.followUp: Write Einstein’s mass-energy equation and state the value of the speed of light in vacuum.

rubric.why: This is the speed of light in vacuum.

modelAnswer: Einstein’s mass-energy equation is E = mc².
The value of c, the speed of light in vacuum, is 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

items.followUp: What is a laboratory thermometer? State its usual temperature range.

rubric.why: A clinical thermometer is designed to measure human body temperature.
rubric.description: Identify what a clinical thermometer measures.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is used to measure human body temperature.

rubric.why: The stated interval gives the usual clinical thermometer range.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the range 35°C to 42°C (or the equivalent Fahrenheit range).

modelAnswer: A clinical thermometer is used to measure human body temperature.
Its range is 35°C to 42°C.

items.followUp: Define boiling point and condensation point, and state how they are related for a substance at a fixed pressure.

rubric.why: Melting point is the temperature at which a solid changes into a liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the temperature at which a solid changes into a liquid.

rubric.why: Freezing point is the temperature at which a liquid changes into a solid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the temperature at which a liquid changes into a solid.

modelAnswer: The melting point is the temperature at which a solid changes into a liquid.
The freezing point is the temperature at which a liquid changes into a solid.
For a given substance at a fixed pressure, its melting point and freezing point are the same temperature.

items.followUp: State Newton’s second law of motion and use it to obtain the relation F = ma for a body of constant mass.

rubric.why: Newton’s second law relates force to the rate of change of momentum.
rubric.description: State the law in terms of momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that force is proportional to the rate of change of momentum and acts in its direction.

rubric.why: This is the mathematical expression of the law when the proportionality constant is one in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for F = Δp/Δt (or the equivalent proportionality statement).

rubric.why: Using momentum p = mv gives the change in momentum for constant mass.
rubric.description: Express the change in momentum for constant mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Δp = m(v − u), or an equivalent use of p = mv.

rubric.why: Substitution gives force as mass times acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for F = m(v − u)/t and/or F = ma.

modelAnswer: Newton’s second law states that the force acting on a body is proportional to the rate of change of its momentum and acts in the direction of the force.
F ∝ Δp/Δt; in SI units, F = Δp/Δt.
For a body of constant mass, p = mv, so Δp = mv − mu = m(v − u).
Therefore, F = m(v − u)/t = ma.

items.followUp: Using a speed-time graph, derive the third equation of motion, v² = u² + 2as.

rubric.why: The graph’s gradient gives acceleration and hence the first equation of motion.
rubric.description: Use the gradient of the speed-time graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining v = u + at from the graph’s slope.

rubric.why: Displacement is the area under the speed-time graph, a trapezium.
rubric.description: Express displacement as the area under the graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for s = ½(u + v)t, or an equivalent area expression.

rubric.why: Substituting the graph-derived velocity relation gives the required displacement equation.
rubric.description: Substitute the velocity relation into the area expression.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for reaching s = ut + ½at².

rubric.why: This is the second equation of motion to be proved.
rubric.description: State the proved second equation of motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final result s = ut + ½at².

modelAnswer: Draw a speed-time graph with time t on the horizontal axis and speed v on the vertical axis; mark the initial speed u at time 0 and the final speed v at time t.
The gradient of the graph is a = (v − u)/t, so v = u + at.
The displacement s is the area under the graph: s = area of trapezium = ½(u + v)t.
Substitute v = u + at: s = ½(u + u + at)t.
Therefore, s = ut + ½at².
